current.text: Portland's season preview projects him to start next to Lillard, Morant, Avdija and Clingan.
His minutes should stay solid. The team likely needs him for about 34 minutes a night, and he must hold 30 or more minutes to keep fantasy value.
Portland has a crowd of on-ball guards. Lillard, Morant and Scoot Henderson all return or arrive, next to Avdija.
Portland is short on forwards. Avdija and Camara are basically the only ones, which protects his minutes.
His usage will probably drop because of all the guards. That leaves him as mainly a steals contributor.
Experts rate him below his market. A rank of 101 is called far too high, and he sits in tier seven among small forwards.
Portland has a new head coach this season.
Minutes and usage are expected to swing from game to game across Portland's rotation.
Portland has three back-to-backs in the fantasy playoffs.

durable.text: Steals are his main fantasy strength. He adds little in the other categories.
His shooting runs in peaks and valleys. Last season he shot poorly until the last six weeks.
He has weak ball handling and is a poor finisher.
He is Portland's only real point-of-attack defender.

note: He is ranked 106 on Yahoo (value 4 USD, average cost 1 USD) and 132 on ESPN (value 0). Last season he cost 4 USD in our league. With 144 players drafted, he is a 1 USD end-of-draft pick at most, and the experts call even a rank near 101 too high. His projected 1.2 steals and 2.0 threes help, but his 44.5% FG and 11.5 points add little. Early in the season, check whether he stays in the starting five and holds 30 or more minutes under the new coach next to Portland's crowded guard group. If he does not, leave him on waivers.
